sum: On May 15, 2026, NextEra Energy, WG Development Corp. and CS Holdco entered into an agreement with Dominion Energy for a two-step merger. The agreement set out Merger Sub Corp.’s merger with Dominion, followed immediately by the surviving corporation’s merger into CS Holdco, subject to specified closing conditions.

NextEra disclosed the agreement in an SEC filing on May 18, 2026, and stated that the first merger remained subject to satisfaction or waiver of closing conditions. The filing provided financial information for incorporation into NextEra’s Securities Act registration statements; the related registration statement became effective July 23, 2026, and definitive proxy materials were filed July 28, 2026.

items.t: NextEra Energy stock gains safeguards as Virginia merger review advances
sum: NextEra Energy and Dominion Energy said on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, that they had strengthened their proposed combination with additional customer and financial protections. In a NextEra Energy news release, the companies said they accepted 101 of 117 conditions proposed by Virginia State Corporation Commission staff and the Office of the Attorney General Division of Consumer Counsel. They accepted another 13 conditions with enhancements or modifications.

The revised package is intended to strengthen Dominion Energy Virginia's financial separation from affiliated businesses, add independent oversight and increase Virginia representation on its board. The companies said the utility would remain locally led and accountable to the Virginia State Corporation Commission while retaining access to NextEra Energy's capital.

The proposal includes four years of shareholder-funded residential bill credits and an additional 100 million US dollars for EnergyShare, which supports energy assistance and weatherization. It also includes 100 million US dollars for workforce development and skilled-trades training.

The companies plan to create 1,000 jobs, including 600 positions at NextEra Energy and about 400 with suppliers, contractors and service providers. They also propose maintaining Dominion Energy's current Virginia employee headcount for at least five years, building a shareholder-funded office tower in downtown Richmond and maintaining dual headquarters.

A new Virginia Supplier Program would support spending of up to 5 billion US dollars with Virginia-based manufacturers, contractors, suppliers and service providers over five years. The commitments are designed to address concerns about customer affordability, employment and the utility's ability to finance future generation, transmission and grid investment.

The companies continue to expect the transaction to close in the second half of 2027, but the proposed combination remains subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions. The filing therefore gives NextEra Energy investors a clearer view of the concessions being offered, while leaving the outcome of the Virginia review unresolved.
The real-time quote of NextEra Energy stock was 79.77 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 14:06 CET on Thursday, November 5, 2026.

sum: Juno Beach, Florida-based NextEra Energy, Inc. (NEE) generates, stores, transmits, distributes, and sells electric power to retail and wholesale customers in North America. The company has a market cap of $175.6 billion and operates through Florida Power & Light Company (FPL) and NEER segments. NextEra generates electricity from wind, solar, nuclear, natural gas, and other clean energy assets.

The electricity supplier's shares have underperformed the broader market over the past year, growing 2.5% compared to the S&P 500 Index's ($SPX) 11.1% surge. Moreover, in 2026, the stock has risen nearly 4.3%, also lagging behind the SPX's 10.7% rise.

Focusing on its industry benchmark, the State Street Utilities Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLU) has fallen 3.2% over the past year, underperforming the stock. In 2026, XLU has grown 1.7% and has also lagged behind the stock.

On Oct. 21, NEE stock declined marginally following the release of its mixed Q3 2026 earnings. The company's revenue for the quarter amounted to $8.1 billion, missing the Street's estimates. However, its adjusted EPS came in at $1.24, which surpassed the consensus estimates. Additionally, NextEra expects full-year earnings in the range of $3.92 to $4.02 per share, which also exceeded analyst forecasts. The stock grew 4.6% in the following trading session.

For the current year, which ends in December, analysts expect NEE's EPS to rise 8.1% to $4.01 on a diluted basis. The company surpassed the consensus estimate in each of the last four quarters, which is impressive.
Among the 20 analysts covering NEE stock, the consensus is a "Moderate Buy." That's based on 11 "Strong Buy" ratings, eight "Holds," and one "Strong Sell."

sum: NextEra Energy came into this Q3 2026 report with a reputation as the clean power bellwether that grows quietly while the market argues about interest rates. The share price reaction looks like relief, but the real story is the strength in profitability rather than a sudden change in narrative.

NextEra Energy Q3 Earnings Beat on FPL Strength, Revenues Miss
sum: NextEra Energy, Inc. NEE reported third-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings of $1.24 per share, up 9.7% from $1.13 a year ago. The figure beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $1.20 by 3.3%. Strong contributions from Florida Power & Light ("FPL") and NextEra Energy Resources supported earnings growth.
GAAP earnings per share were $2.28 compared with $1.18 in the year-ago quarter.
Total operating revenues increased 1.6% year over year to $8.09 billion but missed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $9.08 billion by 10.9%.
NextEra Energy, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | NextEra Energy, Inc. Quote
Operating revenues increased from $7.97 billion in the third quarter of 2025 to $8.09 billion in the reported quarter, primarily supported by higher revenues at FPL.

By segment, FPL generated $5.42 billion in operating revenues, up 2.6% year over year. NextEra Energy Resources contributed $2.52 billion, down 1.9% from the prior-year quarter. Corporate and Other revenues totaled $153 million compared with $115 million a year ago.

FPL reported third-quarter net income of $1.62 billion, up 10.7% from $1.46 billion in the year-ago quarter. Earnings per share increased to 77 cents from 71 cents. Growth was primarily driven by continued disciplined capital investments.
